selected_evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created (LUKS2 format, keyfile, XFS filesystem) and manually verified mountable at /srv/secure before reboot
selected_evidence.summary: Backing file + keyfile created, LUKS2 format applied, XFS built on the mapped device, crypttab/fstab entries added, and the generated srv-secure.mount unit started successfully to prove the boot wiring before reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline captured before restart (boot_id, mount state, marker file)
selected_evidence.summary: Marker file written to /srv/secure, and pre-restart boot_id (377b5195...) plus active mount recorded.
systemctl reboot issued on node1; command returned before the connection dropped, consistent with the node going down for restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
selected_evidence.summary: Node was unreachable during reboot (timeouts then connection resets), then exec access returned with boot_id 0f04bdd9... — different from the pre-restart 377b5195..., proving the OS actually rebooted rather than a service bounce.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked and mounted with no manual intervention, data intact
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/srv_secure, marker.txt content is unchanged, systemd-cryptsetup@srv_secure.service and srv-secure.mount are both active, and journalctl -b shows the cryptsetup unlock and mount happened automatically during this boot with no manual commands run.
